newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-DE SILVA'S 5/85 PUTS SRI LANKA AHEAD OF PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DE SILVA'S 5/85 PUTS SRI LANKA AHEAD OF PAKISTAN.

text.p: Sri Lanka's left-arm seemers Chaminda Vaas and Sajeeva de Silva took nine wickets between them to dismiss Pakistan for 292 by the tea interval on the third day of the second and final test in Colombo on Monday.
Sri Lanka, who made 331, took a first innings lead of 39 runs after capturing the last four Pakistan wickets for 16 runs.
Three of those of those wickets were claimed by de Silva who, in only his second test, bagged five wickets for 85 runs.
The 26-year old fast bowler failed to take a wicket in his only previous test against New Zealand at Hamilton early this year, conceding 65 runs.

Armed with the second new ball, de Silva produced a hostile spell to run through the Pakistani low order, after left-arm spinner Jayantha Silva had dismissed top scorer Moin Khan just two short of his century.
Moin kept the Pakistani batting alive with an exhillerating knock of 98 in 109 balls which included three sixes and nine fours in a stay at the wicket of 175 minutes.

Moin and Asif Mujtaba, who missed his half century by one run, put on 91 for the sixth wicket. Mujtaba was out in the third over after lunch pulling a long hop from Vaas to long-leg where Aravinda de Silva took a fine running catch diving to his left.
The left-hander, who batted a long 274 minutes, hit seven fours.
Moin was caught at backward point when he attempted to reach his century with a back cut off Jayantha Silva.
It was Sajeeva de Silva who cleaned up the tail, after Pakistan had looked bouyant in the morning session losing only one wicket and putting on 90.
Scores: Sri Lanka all out for 331. Pakistan all out for 292.
